steps.observation: You have 30 seconds. Explain the difference between RNA and DNA.

steps.action:
DNA  
• Sugar: deoxyribose (lacks one oxygen).  
• Bases: A, T, C, G (contains thymine).  
• Structure: usually double-stranded, long, stable helix.  
• Role: long-term storage of genetic information; mostly stays in the nucleus (eukaryotes).

RNA  
• Sugar: ribose (has an extra oxygen).  
• Bases: A, U, C, G (uracil replaces thymine).  
• Structure: usually single-stranded, shorter, less stable; can fold into many shapes.  
• Role: temporary copies (mRNA), translators (tRNA, rRNA), regulators, catalysts; found in nucleus and cytoplasm.

Bottom line: DNA is the durable archive; RNA is the versatile, short-lived working copy and toolset.
